title: Change Detector & Channel Fabric for Evals Quality Alerts
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a defensible link between changes (model/config/quantization) and evals-quality signals, and deliver a channel fabric in Console that routes consolidated, context-rich alerts to Slack and PagerDuty while minimizing noisy duplicates.

Background: We see periodic spikes from evals when teams try new quantization profiles or change prompt templates. Current alerts are noisy and disconnected from the underlying change that caused them. This ticket implements a change detector that fingerprints commits/config diffs and a channel fabric that maps a change fingerprint -> alert policy, enabling: contextual messages, automatic grouping, temporal suppression and sticky dedupe across Slack/PagerDuty.

Scope:
- Change detector service (lightweight) that consumes model/config rollouts (webhook + Console events) and produces a canonical fingerprint for each rollout.
- Enrich evals regression alerts with fingerprint + rollout metadata (author, id, model_variant, diff_summary).
- Channel fabric in Console: rule editor for mapping fingerprints/tags to Slack channels and PD escalation policies.
- Deduplication strategy: deterministic grouping key + decay window + signature similarity threshold.
- Integration tests and a canary: roll out to internal teams first, then opt-in customers.

Out of scope: automatic remediation, deep root-cause ML explainers (separate follow-up with Research).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Alerts generated by evals include change_fingerprint and human-readable diff_summary.
2) Console UI exposes a Channel Fabric editor where PMs can bind fingerprint patterns to channels/policies.
3) Slack notifications consolidate regressions from the same fingerprint into a single thread (or updated message) for a 48-hour window.
4) PagerDuty incidents are created only when a fingerprint's first critical regression occurs; subsequent same-fingerprint regressions within decay window annotate the existing incident instead of creating new ones.
4) End-to-end test run for internal canary and documentation for customer onboarding.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: the detector runs as a small service in the control plane. It subscribes to model/config rollout events (Console webhook), computes: {rolled_files_hash, prompt_template_hash, quant_profile_hash, model_sha, timestamp, author} and then reduces to a canonical fingerprint (sha256 of normalized diff). We store recent fingerprints with TTL and similarity indexes (minhash or tokenized diff heuristics) to handle near-duplicate changes.

Dedupe algorithm: primary key = "fingerprint"; fallback = model_variant + top-3 changed files + time_bucket. Use a 48-hour strong-suppression window by default, configurable per-fabric-rule. Slack path uses message update/threading via chat.update; PD path annotates existing incidents via PD REST API (incident key = fingerprint).

Privacy/SEC: diff summaries must avoid including PII or customer data; only retreive config metadata and non-sensitive diffs. Security review flagged (see dependencies).
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal): run detector for internal rollouts only; route to #evals-internal Slack and a dedicated PD escalation policy. Validate dedupe behavior with synthetic regressions.
Phase 2 (beta): allow customer teams to opt into Channel Fabric routing in Console; provide toggle and docs.
Phase 3 (GA): enable defaults for orgs that opt-in via admin setting.
Rollback: ability to disable fabric rule or disable enrichment pipeline; alerts revert to pre-enriched behavior.
telemetry_requirements:
Emit events: fingerprint.created, fingerprint.matched, alert.enriched, channel.route_decision (rule_id), dedupe.action = {create|annotate|suppress}, pd.incident_annotated, slack.thread_updated. Include latency metrics and failure counts. Store 90d retention for audit.
SLOs: enrichment path 99th latency < 300ms; route decision success rate > 99%.
test_plan:
Unit tests for fingerprint normalization (deterministic), similarity heuristics. Integration tests: simulate model/config rollout -> eval regression -> verify console enrichment, Slack thread update and PD incident annotation. Load test: 500 changes/hour to validate TTL index and performance.
Acceptance: run synthetic regression suite end-to-end and verify dedupe windows and channel mapping behave per policy.
